- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥1.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-1.5), model underestimates; adjust downward bias by +3–5% to align with true trend.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the 10–15 day horizon after a spike; add 2–4% to forecast for that window.
- Model overestimates early in 30-day forecast when sentiment is volatile; cap forecast at 10% above recent 7-day average.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 14-day average, reduce by 5–8% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a negative spike, model often misses the rebound; add 3–5% to forecast 3–5 days after sentiment shift.
